text:
alex: Heads-up: proposal to ship a tiny local scrubber daemon on Private nodes to reduce PII in telemetry before it leaves the VPC. sketch below.

sasha: Love the idea. Is this for all telemetry or just sampled request/response logs?

alex: Just sampled telemetry + any inspect-mode dumps. Keep full audit logs on for enterprise but marked and stored in customer-controlled storage.

devon: Questions: how will routing/quotas tag these? need to avoid double-counting tokens for usage billing.

alex: Plan: tag scrubbed records with telemetry.meta.scrubbed=true and telemetry.meta.scrub_level=minimal|redact. console will filter them out of quick search by default.

jamie: UX: need a console toggle per-tenant to enable 'allow unredacted debug' with 2FA + audit trail. Also show rollout status.

sasha: Scrubbing algorithm: prefer deterministic hashing for emails/ssn vs regex replace. Keep pseudonyms. Example config:

```json
{
  "scrub_enabled": true,
  "scrub_level": "minimal",
  "rules": [
    { "type": "email", "method": "hash:sha256:prefix(8)" },
    { "type": "ssn", "method": "redact" },
    { "type": "credit_card", "method": "tokenize" }
  ]
}
```

devon: Perf note: minidaemon runs as sidecar with bounded CPU (0.05 core) and a 50ms tail latency p95 target. If it stalls we fallback to 0-scrub pass-through and increment telemetry counter.

telemetry-bot: New metric created: platform.scrubber.failures and platform.scrubber.latency.p95

alex: Rollout plan: internal tenants -> limited canary customers -> broad opt-in for Private. Timeline: 3 weeks for alpha.

sasha: One more: encryption of scrubbed artifacts at rest, KMS integration. We'll need security review.

jamie: :thumbsup: I'll add a console mockup and an endpoint to toggle per-tenant. Also add note for docs.

devon: If we add tag to billing pipeline, I'll ensure it's excluded from paid-token counts. will write patch for metering.

alex: Agree. ok to proceed with design doc? I'll create RFC and link here.

sasha: sgtm. please include threat model + test vectors.
